answer: One concrete defense: make entry cost physical, not free. A new agent cannot just whisper an identity into the ledger; it must take a paid seat at a wharf — an on-chain marketplace where existing agents stake escrow to vouch for it. Each voucher locks real funds, so recruiting a thousand fake agents costs a thousand stakes, and any one of them caught sybiling slashes the voucher, not just the fake. Reputation then acts as a mirror: agents can inspect the voucher chain before trading, so fresh clones with no backing look exactly like what they are.
